case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 18-1-2010 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4785 of 2003).
full_judgment:
Borhanuddin, J: This civil appeal by leave arose out of the judgment and order dated 18-1-2010 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4785 of 2003 affirming the judgment and decree dated 14-8-2003 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Chittagong, in Other Appeal No.365 of 2002 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 24-7-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong, in Other Suit No.225 of 1990 decreeing the suit.
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal are that Hazi Azama Khatun Chowdhurani, predecessor of the respondent Nos. 1-3 herein, as plaintiff instituted Other Suit No.179 of 1980 for partition on 24-12-1980 impleading Mst. Selina Begum and others as defendants and by subsequent amendment the plaintiff added another prayer for declaration that the registered Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 executed by some of the heirs of Monu Meah infavour of the defendant No.1 is void, contending inter alga, that the lands of RS Plot Nos.126 and 127 of Mouza-Kashim Bazar, under Police Station-Kotwali, Chittagong, recorded in RS Khatian No.77 originally belonged to one Abdul Hamid who died leaving two sons namely Abdul Aziz and Abdul Motalib and three daughters namely Amena Khatun, Momena Khatun, Siraj Khatun and one wife Hajera Khatun; On the death of Hajeta Khatun her sons and daughters inherited her share; Subsequently, on the basis of amicable partition, Arnena Khatun in her share got exclusively 16(sixteen) Gondas land from the western part of RS Plot No.127; Amena Khatun leased out her land to MA Quader and Monu Meah by registered patty dated 21-1-1954; Said land increased by `Gunjaish’ to 18(eighteen) Gondas 1(one) Kora equivalent to 0.3688 acre which was marked as PS Plot No.81 and was recorded in the name of MA Quader and Monu Meah in PS Khatian No.10 of Mouza-Kashim Bazar; Said MA Quader sold his share to defendant No.2 Sultana Begum by registered kabala deeds in 1964 and the rest 10(ten) Gondas 1(one) Kora land was in the share of Monu Meah who died leaving two wives namely Chernon Bahar and Nurjahan Begum, six sons namely Md Nasir, Md Yousuf, Gulzar Hossain, Ahmed Hossain, Akter Hossain, Md Ishaque and one daughter Anjuman Ara. In the BS Map the land of Monu Meah was marked as Plot No.29 measuring an area of 0.21 acre of land; Plaintiff Hazi Azama Khatun Chowdhurarti purchased the land of Monu Meah from his heirs by registered Kabala Deed Nos.7835, 7885 and 7886 all dated 14-5-1980 and got possession. A few dates after purchase by the plaintiff, husband of the defendant No.1 disclosed that he purchased the suit land from the heirs of Monu Meah and threatened the plaintiff to dispossess from the land for which the plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No.308 of 1990 for perpetual injunction. During pendency of the said suit the defendant No.1 and her husband trespassed into some portion of land of the plaintiff. On 14-12-1980 by obtaining copy of the sale deed the plaintiff came to know that the defendant No.1 has purchased some land from some of the heirs of Monu Meah and wives of Monu Meah without obtaining permission from the District Judge and executed sale deed infavour of the wife of the defendant No.1 for an on behalf of minors.
3. Thereafter, the plaintiff withdraw her suit and on 20-12-1980 requested the defendant No.1 for amicable partition but the defendant No.1 and her husband refused and therefore she was constrained to file the suit for partition firstly claiming 6(six) Gondas 1(one) Kora 2(two) Krantis 4½ (four and a half) Dentis land out of 10(ten) Gondas 2(two) Koras of BS Plot No.29 but subsequently by amending the plaint on 9-7-1995 the plaintiff raised her claim to the entire 10(ten) Gondas 2(two) Koras land and by such amendment she also prayed for further relief of declaration that registered Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 is illegal and void.
4. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint and contending, interalia, that MA Quader and Monu Meah while owning and possessing 18½ (eighteen and a half) Gondas of land of RS Plot Nos.126 and 127 executed an agreement for sale on 31-5-1964 infavour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and delivered possession thereof on receipt of earnest money; MA Quader registered the sale deed on 31-12-1964 infavour of the defendant No.2 but Monu Meah died before execution and registration of the sale deed leaving behind six sons, one daughter and two wives of whom four sons and one daughter were minors. MA Quader and Monu Meah were recorded as tenants in RS Khatian No.77 Plot No.127 and as Malik of corresponding 1'S Plot No.81 recorded in PS Khatian No.10 of Mouza-Kashim Bazar for an area of 16(sixteen) Gondas plus Gunjaish 2(two) Gondas 2(two) Koras in total 18(eighteen) Gondas 2(two) Koras land; On 31-5-1964, MA Quader and Monu Meah jointly entered a contract to sell their entire land to the defendant No.1 and 2 for a total price of Rs.28,000 and on receipt of a part payment of Rs.7,000 delivered possession of the land to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. As per contract MA Quader sold his 8(eight) Gondas land to Sultana Begum, the defendant No.2, who is mother of the defendant No.1; Unfortunately, shortly after the contract for sale, Monu Meah became ill and thereafter died leaving two widows namely Chemon Bahar (defendant No.10) and Nurjahan Begum and three sons the defendants No.5-7 by Chernon Bahar and three sons i.e. Md Nasir and the defendant Nos. 4 and S and one daughter the defendant No.9 by Nurjahan Begum„ due to illness and then death of Monu Meah, the defendant No.1 could not get her purchase deed executed or registered; Md Nasir and the defendant No.4 Md Yousuf, in part performance of their father's contract for sale dated 31-5-1964, sold their share of the land measuring 2(two) Gondas 1(one) Kora 4.2 Krantis to the defendant No.1 by registered kabala deed executed on 15-9-1966 and registered on 16-9-1966 and handed over, amongst others, the original lease deed by which their father and MA Quader acquired the land; The said Chemon Bahar and Nurjahan Begum, widows of Monu Meah, sold their share in the land, in part performance of Monu Meah's contract for sale, by registered Kabala Deed No.8567 dated 28-6-1967; For getting sale deed for the rest part of the land the defendant No.1 on 30-8-1967 instituted Other Suit No.57 of 1967 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong for Specific Performance of Contract against the defendant Nos. 5-9, who were represented by their respective mothers; Mothers of the minors appeared in the suit on behalf of their minor sons and daughter, filed written statement in court but ultimately did not contest and the suit was decreed ex-parte on 25-6-1969; On 25-6-1969, the defendant No.1 deposited the balance consideration money in court vide Challan No.4505 dated 25-6-1969; The defendant No.5 withdrew Rs.1341.50 from court vide Court's Order No.21 dated 26-8-1972; The remaining heirs of Monu Meah i.e. the defendant Nos. 5-9 by registered Sale Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 sold their share of the land to the defendant No.1 in compliance of the decree passed in Other Suit No.57 of 1967 and withdrew the balance consideration money deposited in court through Payment Order passed by Court's Order No.22 dated 17-12-197, it may be noted that, at the time of execution and registration of the Kabala Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974, Md Ishaque son of Monu Meah and Chemon Bahar and Most. Anjurrian, Ara, daughter of Monu Meah and Nurjahan Begum being minors, their mothers executed the kabala deed on behalf of the minors with reference to the decree of the court; By the said 3 kabala deeds the defendant No.1 acquired title on the entire 10(ten) Gondas and 2(two) Koras land of Monti Meah and had been possessing the same since the contract of 1964; The defendant No.1 spent about Taka 60,000 for removing hill rocks, levelling the land, construction of pucca boundary wall, Iron Gate at the entrance, RCC Slab on the drain alongside the road, two houses etc.; The defendant No.1 obtained electricity supply connection and water supply line and paid rents and bills regularly; The defendant No.1 also got construction plan approved from the CDA and applied for loan from House Building Finance Corporation and was taking preparation for construction of the building; By amicable arrangement with her mother defendant No.2, the defendant No.1 got her share of the land from Western side of the plot; In the BS survey the suit land has been recorded correctly in the name of the defendant No.1; When the defendant No.1 was about to start construction of residential building on the land, the plaintiff instituted a suit for perpetual injunction and lastly the present suit on fraudulent claim; In the meantime, the defendant No.1 died leaving behind her husband Dr. BM Fayzur Rahman and two sons and three daughters, who were substituted in the suit as defendant Nos. 1(Ka) to i(Cha) in the suit; Subsequently, the substituted defendant No.1(Kha) died leaving behind one widow and one son, who were substituted as defendant Nos. 1(Ka) and (Kha); The said heirs on 5-4-1995 submitted an additional written statement contending, interalia, that after entering contract to sell Monu Meah has claimed an excess amount of Taka 2,500 for the excess land called 'Gunjaishi; Advance money of Taka 7,000 plus excess Taka 2,500 in total Taka 9,500 was paid by the defendant No.1 to Monu Meah by Cheque Nos. AD 9882 dated 3-6-1964 and CAD 1964 dated 24-11-1964 drawn on the present Janata Bank, Agrabad Branch, Chitta-gong which he has encashed; The defendant No.1 has obtained hill cutting permission from the Chittagong Development Authority vide Plan No.A02512/ 76163-64/310 dated 16-9- 1964.
5. Defendant No.1 in her written statement filed on 1-7-1981 denied claim of title and possession of the plaintiff and contending, interalia, that she and her daughter jointly entered a contract on 31-5-1964 with MA Quader and Monu Meah to purchase their land on part payment of Rs.7,000 and got possession of the property on the date of the contract and since then they are in possession of the land; On receipt of the balance consideration money of his part MA Quader sold his share to the defendant No.2 by registered kabala deed dated 31-12-1964 but due to illness and subsequent death of Monu Meah the defendant No.1 could not get kabala deed executed or registered; Heirs of Monu Meah or the plaintiff are not in possession of any part of the suit land and the kabala deeds of the plaintiff are collusive, fraudulent and sham transactions; After death of Monu Meah his heirs sold the land of Monu Meah to the defendant No.1 by registered kabala deeds and he is in possession of the said part of the ]and from west side of the plot.
6. Defendant No.2 Sultana Begum contested the suit by filing a written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint and contending interalia, that Arnena Khatun transferred 16(sixteen) Gondas of land from RS Plot No.127 appertaining to RS Khatian No.77; There was about 21/2 (two and a half) Gondas of land in access of 16(sixteen) Gorillas within specific boundaries made by the brick built pillars and possession was delivered to MA Quader and Monu Meah vide lease deed dated 21-1-1954 and the said MA Quader and Monu Meah entered into a contract to sell the land to these defendant and defendant No.1 and executed sale agreement on 31-5-1964 on receipt of advance consideration of money of Taka 7,000 encash and put them in possession in part performance of contract and since them the defendants are in possession of the suit schedule property; Thereafter, MA Quader executed kabala and registered the same on 31- 12-1964 for his share with Gunjaish; Monu Meah could not execute and register sale deed infavour of the defendant No.1 due to his illness and death; But subsequently all his legal heirs executed and registered sate deed infavour of the defendant No.1 and sold their entire share of about 10(ten) Gondas 2(two) Koras of land; Thus, the entire right, title, interest and possession of MA Quader and Monu Meah devolved upon the defendants and BS Khatian stands in their name; By amicable partition this defendant is in possession of the eastern part of the PS Plot No.81 while the defendant No.1 is in possession on the western part of the said plot; After purchase these defendants developed the land as per approved plan vide CDA; The plaintiff suit is liable to be dismissed.
7. Added defendant No.3 by filing written statement contested the suit denying material allegation made in the plaint and contending, interalia, that his father Dr. Abu Jafar purchased the share of MA Quader measuring 7(seven) Gondas 2(two) Koras land in the benami of his grandmother, the defendant No.2; His father Dr. Abu Jafar died in 1975 and on 29-5-1982 the defendant No.2 in presence of all of her other children gifted her 7(seven) Gondas 2(two) Koras land to the defendant No.3 by registered deed of gift No.21426 and gave possession to him and he got the said land mutated in his name but husband of the defendant No.1 intentionally inserted BS Plot No.75/29 in the said deed of gift; Husband of the defendant No.1 made a kitchen and took water supply line on the Western side of the land and when asked he had promised to shift it to the Eastern side; Report of Advocate Commissioner Mr Sanaullah is not true and the defendant No.3 is not bound by that report and if there be any Cunjaish, the defendant No.3 is entitled to half of it.
8. Defendant Nos. 4, 5, 7 and 8 also contested the suit by filing a joint separate written statement contending, interalia, that Monu Meah was the owner in possession of 0.2100 acre land of BS Plot No.29, who levelled the land cutting hill rock and therefore it was recorded as Bhiti land in RS Khatian; They are four sons out of seven children of Monu lvfeah and Monu Meah did not enter any contract on 31-5-1964 to sell his land as claimed by the defendant No.1; By amendment of written statement on 16-4-2001, the said defendants denied that heirs of Monu Meah sold the lands to the defendant No.1 by registered Kabala deeds; The ex-park decree passed in Other Suit No.57 of 1967 was fraudulent and collusive; None of the defendants executed the Kabala Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 and the defendant No.1 did not get any title or possession in the suit land.
9. After hearing the parties and perusing the evidence on record, the trial Court decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 24-7-2002 in preliminary form giving (a) 9¼ (nine and one-fourth) Gondas land to the plaintiff, (b) the defendant No.3 will get the rest 9¼ (nine and one-fourth) Gondas land provided he pays
court fee and (c) the decree passed in Other Suit No.57 of 1967 was collusive, fraudulent and not bounding upon the plaintiff.
10. Against the judgment and decree, the defendant Nos. 1 (Ka) and 1 (Ga) preferred Other Appeal No.365 of 2002 in the Court of District Judge, Chittagong, which on transfer was heard by the learned Additional District Judge of the 6th Court, Chittagong who by judgment and decree dated 14-8-2003 dismissed the appeal.
11. Being aggrieved, the defendant Nos. 1(Ka) and l(Ga) preferred Civil Revision No.4785 of 2003 in the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which was initially issued by a Single Bench but subsequently it was detected that at the relevant time it was within the jurisdiction of a Division Bench and, as such, a fresh Rule was obtained in Civil Rule No.253(R) of 2007 and this Rule was finally heard as Civil Rule and the Civil Revision No.4785 was discharged after contested hearing by a Single Bench of the High Court Division vide judgment and order dated 18-1-2010.
12. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order, the defendant Nos. 1(Ka) and l(Ga) preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1843 of 2010 before this Division and obtained leave on 23-4-2015 which has been registered as instant Civil Appeal No.221 of 2015.
13. Mr M. Quinrul Haque Siddique, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the courts below failed to consider that heirs of Monu Meah did not take any step to assail or set-aside the sale deed executed by them even after knowledge but the plaintiff obtained registered deeds from them and, as such, the plaintiff did not acquire any title or possession in the suit land because the heirs of Monu Meah after losing title sold the land by three kabala deeds in 1980 and therefore the judgment and decree passed by the Courts below are liable to be set-aside. He also submits that the courts below committed an error of law as well as facts in not considering that the registered Kabala Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 (Exhibit 2) executed by the defendant Nos. 5, 6 and 7 when they were major alongwith two minors Md Ishaque and Anjuman Ara Begum represented by their custodian and natural guardian mother, the defendant Nos. 5-7 did not file any suit for cancellation of the said registered sale deed within the time framed for such suit, of them the defendant Nos. 4, 5, 7 and 8 filed written statement in the suit denying sale, but neither the plaintiff nor the contesting defendant Nos. 4, 5, 7 and 8 takes any step in the suit to disprove the signature of the defendant No.4 on the Exhibit No.A-1 and those of the defendant Nos. 5-7 on Exhibit No.2, moreover, out of them only the defendant No.5 examined himself as DW 1 and in his cross examination at first he admitted his signature on the registered deed dated 12-10-1974 but thereafter he denied the same and without considering this evidence the suit was decreed and affirmed by the lower Appellate and Revisional Court which is liable to be set-aside. He further submits that the defendant No.1 in her written statement very specifically stated that she has purchased the entire share of land of Monu Meah measuring 101/2 (ten and a half) Gondas land from the heirs of Monu Meah by three registered kabala deeds of 1980, the defendant No.1 asserted that by Kabala Deed No.5078 dated 15-9-1966 (Exhibit No. A-1) executed by Md Nasir and Md Yousuf both sons of Monu Meah and by Kabala Deed No.8567 dated 28-6-1967 (Exhibit A) executed by Most. Chemon Bahar and Nurjahan Begum, wives of deceased Monu Meah had purchased the share of those heirs but in the plaint no allegation as against the said two kabala deeds have been raised by the plaintiff to challenge those transfers, even there is no evidence at all on record to disbelieve those two sale deeds. Despite, in absence of pleading and evidence, the courts below have assailed purchase of land by the defendant by those two kabala deeds which is not only non-application of judicial mind but also error of law resulting error in the decision occasioning failure of justice when the entire share of Monu Meah has been given in the saham of the plaintiff.
14. Mr Mustafa Niaz Muhammad, learned Advocate for the respondent No.5 (added defendant No.3 of the suit) submits that father of the respondent No.5 Late Dr. Abu Jafar purchased half of the Plot No.127 from MA Quader in the benami of his mother defendant No.2 Sultana Begum and thereafter, said Sultana Begum transferred the land infavour of his grandson respondent No.5 vide deed of gift dated 21-6-1982 and since then the respondent No.5 is in possession of the land with Gunjaish. He also submits that above facts is not disputed by any of the party as such the respondent No.5 is entitled to get saham in the land of Plot No.127 belonged to MA Quader.
15. On the other hand, learned advocate for respondent Nos. 1-3 in support of the impugned judgment and order submits that three purchase deeds infavour of the plaintiff are admitted by the executants of the deeds i.e. heirs of Monu Meah by filing written statement and DW 1 Gulzar Hossain son of Monu Meah in his deposition also admitted execution of sale deeds infavour of the plaintiff as such the courts below correctly arrived at a finding that the plaintiff has right, title and interest over the suit land. He also submits that execution of alleged deeds infavour of the defendant No.1 for the self-same suit land are denied by the so-called executants of those deeds as well as by the plaintiff and perusing evidence on record, courts below rightly came to a conclusion that those deeds do not create any right, title and interest infavour of the defendant No.1. He again submits that alleged bainanama dated 31-5-1964 was not produced in Other Suit No. 57 of 1967 nor in the present suit as such courts below rightly found that the defendant No.1 failed to prove the alleged contract for sale. Learned Advocate further submits that though the plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1-3 are not a party of the fraudulent sale deeds, Exhibit A, A-1 and A-2, but they are entitled to seek remedy by instituting present suit as per provision of section 28 (2) (b) of the Registration Act read with section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Ranbir Purkayas-Jha @ Bhanu vs Alekjan Bibi and others reported in 34 DLR (AD) 98, the case of Most Rokeya Khatun vs Alijan Alijan Bepari and others reported in 34 DLR (AD) 266, the case of Siddique Ahmed Chowdhury and others vs Gani Ahmed and others reported in 33 DLR (AD) 1, the case of Syed Kawsar Ali vs Gahar Kazi and others reported in 37 DLR (AD) 177, the case of Cinmoy Chowdhury and others vs Sree Mridul Chowdhury and others reported in 2003 BLD (AD) 83 = 55 DLR (AD) 115, the case of Md Siddique vs Bhupendra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and others reported in 13 DLR 544, the case of Shahani Bibi being dead her heirs: Mohammad Azim and others vs Nur Islam being dead his heirs: Doty Islam and others reported in 4 BLC 195, the case of Anwarul Azim and others vs Fatema Khatoon and others (unreported) being CP No. 1059 of 2004, the case of Md Alkas Ali and others vs Mansur Ahmed Khan and others reported in 1983 BLD (AD) 126, the case of Altab Hossain Sikder and others vs Abdul Malek Sikder and others reported in 23 BLC (AD) 64 and the case of Mafizuddin Khan vs Jadu Pramanik and others reported in 11 DLR 424.
16. Heard the learned advocates for the respective party and perused the papers/ documents contained in the paper book.
17. It appears from the record that the predecessor of respondents Hazi Azama Khatun Chowdhurani as plaintiff filed instant suit for declaration of title, partition of the suit land and also for further declaration that registered Sale Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 and ex-parte decree dated 5-7-1969 passed in the Other Suit No.57 of 1967 are not bound by them.
18. Contesting defendant No.1 by filing a written statement claimed that plaintiff has/had no possession over the suit land, as such, the suit is not maintainable without seeking the relief of recovery of khas possession and the suit is barred by the proviso of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act.
19. 7(seven) issue were framed by the trial Court to try the suit. Issue No.4 was "is the suit maintainable in its present form?"
20. Plaintiff claimed that earlier she filed a suit for Permanent Injunction against the present defendant No.1 relating to the suit land. In Paragraph Nos.6 and 7 of the plaint of present suit the plaintiff stated that:
“……. during pendency of injunction suit, the defendant Nod's husband trespassed into some portion of the Schedule No.1 land taking helpless condition of the lady plaintiff ……….”
21. PW 1 in his examination-in-chief deposed as follows:
“………. ১নং বিবাদীর স্বামী কিছু অংশ হইতে আমাদেরকে বেদখল করেন ……… ”
22. Thus, dispossession of the plaintiff from a portion of the suit land being admitted, the plaintiff was required by law to seek relief of recovery of khas possession which she did not and, as such, simple suit for declaration without seeking relief for recovery of khas possession is not tenable inasmuch as proviso of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act mandates that no Court shall make any such declaration where the plaintiff, being able to seek further relief than a mere declaration of title, omits to do so and without considering this factual and legal aspect courts below committed an error of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.
23. The plaintiff claimed that she purchased entire share of Monu Meah measuring 10 (ten and a half) Gondas land from the heirs of Monu Meah by three kabala deeds of 1980. On the other hand, the defendant No.1 asserted that by Kabala Deed No.5078 dated 15-9-1966 (Exhibit No. A-1) executed by Md Nasir and Md Yousuf both sons of Monu Meah and by Kabala Deed No.8567 dated 28-6-1967 (Exhibit No.A) executed by Most. Chemon Bahar and Nurjahan Begum, wives of deceased Monu Meah she purchased the share of those heirs. But in the plaint no allegation as against the said two kabala deeds has been raised by the plaintiff to challenge those transfers. Even there is no evidence at all on record to disbelieve those two sale deeds. In total absence of pleading and evidence, the courts below have assailed purchase of land by the defendants by those two kabala deeds. It is not only non-application of judicial mind but also error of law resulting error in the decision occasioning failure of justice when the entire share of Monu Meah has been given in the saham of the plaintiff.
24. It is pertinent to mention here that, whether it is a deed or a decree, if it stands as a hurdle to get a declaration of title, the same hurdle is to be removed as per provision of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act in the name of consequential relief inasmuch as through that deed or decree the right, title or interest of the plaintiff is denying or interested to deny.
25. This Division in the case of Dudu Mia and others vs Ekram Miah Chowdhury and others, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 7, held:
"So, in a case where plaintiff is a party to a document or decree that has clouded his title to the property in suit, he is to seek declaration either of the way, i.e. that the document or decree is void or void ab initio or that for declaration as well as for cancellation. In the absence of seeking a declaration as against such document or decree he cannot have a declaration merely in respect of his title in respect of the property in suit even if he contends that his suit is not barred as per provision of section 42 of the Specific relief Act."
26. From the discussions made above, it is apparent that the instant suit relating to the prayer for declaration of title is not maintainable without seeking any relief against two above mentioned deeds as per the proviso of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act.
27. Another contention of the respondent-plaintiff is that the judgment and decree passed in Other Class Suit No.57 of 1967 as well as the Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 is not binding upon them.
28. The trial court observed in his judgment and decree that the existence of the Other Class Suit No.57 of 1967 is questionable and the defendant of instant suit failed to produce any evidence from which it can be established that the alleged contract for sale was proved in the Suit No.57 of 1967.
29. Relevant portion of the judgment and decree of the trial court is quoted below:
“প্রদর্শনী-সি (২) হইতেছে প্রথম সাব-জজ আদালতের অপর ৫৭/৬৭ নং মোকদ্দমার ডিক্রী সহি মুহুরী নকল। উক্ত প্রদঃ সি (২) অনুসারে দেখা যায় যে, উক্ত পূর্বে সুলতানা বেগম, দক্ষিণে জুটমিলের ডাইরেকটারের বাস-ভবন, পূর্বে এম, এ, খান এবং পশ্চিমে ডাইরেকটারের বাসভবনের রাস্তা। ৪ ১/২ গন্ডা ভূমির জন্য উক্ত মোকদ্দমা করা হইয়াছিল। যদি ৪ ১/২ গন্ডা ভূমির জন্য উক্ত চৌহদ্দি সঠিক হয় তাহা হইলে মনু মিয়ার ২ পুত্রের নিকট হইতে প্রদঃ এ (১) ১৬-৯-৬৬ ইং তারিখে ২ গন্ডা ১ কড়া ভূমি এবং ২৮-৬-৬৭ ইং তারিখ মনু মিয়ার ২ স্ত্রীর নিকট হইতে যে ২ গন্ডা ভূমি খরিদ করিয়াছিলেন তাহা কোন দিকে। অর্থাৎ কবলা পাওয়ার মোকদ্দমা দায়েরের পূর্বে মনু মিয়া ও ওয়ারিশগণের নিকট হইতে ১নং বিবাদীনি ৪ গন্ডা ১ কড়া জমি খরিদ করিয়াছিলেন। অতএব অপর ৫৭/৬৭ নং মোকদ্দমা দায়ের কালে মোকদ্দমায় যে চৌহদ্দি প্রদান করা হইয়াছে তাহাতে অবশ্যই যে কোন একদিকে ১নং বিবাদীনির অস্তিত্ পাওয়া যাইত। কিন্তু বাস্তবে তাহা না থাকায় যদি ৫৭/৬৭ নং মোকদ্দমার চৌহদ্দির বিশ্বাস করা যায় তাহা হইলে প্রদঃ এ, এ(১) এর অস্তিত্ব বা কার্যকারিতা অবিশ্বাস করিতে হয়। পাশাপাশিভাবে উক্ত দলিল দুইটি বিশ্বাস করিলে অপর ৫৭/৬৭ নং মোকদ্দমাটির অস্তিত্ব অবিশ্বাস করিতে হয়।
১নং বিবাদীনি মনু মিয়ার সঙ্গে বায়না করিয়াছিলেন এই মর্মে বায়নানামা ৫৭/৬৭ নং মোকদ্দমায় প্রমাণ হইয়াছিল কিনা তত্মর্মে কোন প্রমাণাদি ১নং বিবাদী আদালতে দাখিল করেন নাই।”

30. But on perusal of Exhibits C, Cl and C2 i.e. the order sheet of the Other Class Suit No.57 of 1967 it is apparent that the present defendant No.1 as plaintiff instituted the said suit in the Court of 1st Sub-Ordinate Judge, Chittagong, for specific performance of contract and the mothers of defendants of the said suit appeared on behalf of their minor children as guardian and filed written statement but ultimately did not contest. Thereafter, the said suit was decreed ex-parte and the defendants of the suit were directed to execute a sale deed in favour of the decree holder of the suit who is the defendant No.1 in the instant suit. Furthermore, on perusal of Exhibits C, C-1 and C-2 it is apparent that the decree holder of the Suit No.57 of 1967 had deposited the consideration money of the contract for sale in the court concern and the deposited consideration money was withdrawn by the defendants of the Suit No.57 of 1967. So, said transaction proved that the contract for sale as well as the decree of the Suit No. 57 of 1967 are acted upon and the Suit No.57 of 1967 is well existed.
31. Furthermore, none of the parties of the Suit challenged the judgment and decree of Other Suit No.57 of 1967. In this suit it has been proved well that none of the executants of Exhibits A, A-1 and A-2 raised any objection anywhere against the genuineness of these deeds after they attained majority, even the defendants of Other Class Suit No.57 of 1967 also did not challenge that decree after they attained majority. In the circumstances, the courts below committed wrong in finding these Exhibits A, A-1 and A-2 void and not acted 'upon at the instance of the plaintiff who claim to have purchased the suit land long after purchase of the same by the defendants. The defendants' purchase deeds Exhibits A, A-1 and A-2 are all much earlier than that of the plaintiff and there is no evidence or facts and circumstances at all to prove that the executants of these deeds ever raised any objection against the validity of these deeds and in the circumstances the courts below committed illegality in decreeing the suit of the plaintiff allocating the purchased land of the defendant to the share of the plaintiff.
32. Defendant No.4 name;v Gulzar Hossain who is the heir of Menu Meah deposed as DW 1 and admits in his cross-examination that:
“…………… বায়নানামা মূলে চুক্তি প্রবলের মোকদ্দমা হয়। ৩১-৫-৬৪ ইং তারিখ আব্দুল কাদের ও মনু মিয়া
১/২নং বিবাদীর নিকট ভূমি বিক্রয়ের জন্য বায়নাপত্র সম্পাদন করে।…………”
33. Pursuant to the contract for sale executed by Monu Meah, the heirs of Monu Meah executed two separate Deed being Nos. 8567 and 5078 dated 28-6-1967 and 15-9-1966 which are marked as Exhibits A and A-1 respectively. In this regard it is pertinent to mention here that neither the plaintiff of the instant suit nor the executants of Deed Nos. 8567 and 5078 deny those deeds. On perusal of Exhibit A-1 (Deed No.5078 dated 15-9-1966) it appears that Monu Meah entered into a contract with the present defendant No.1 for
sale of a portion of the suit land. The recital of the said deed proved that the contract for sale was executed between Monu Meah and the present defendant No.1.
34. For proper appreciation the relevant portion of the Deed No.5078 dated 15-9-1966 is reproduced below:
“……….. And whereas the said land of the schedule of the above lease deed were seized and possessed by Monu Meah and MA Quader equally and they executed a sale agreement with the purchaser and Mrs. Sultana Begum on 31-5-1964, fixing the price of the above whole land of the schedule of the lease deed for consideration a sum of Rs.28,000 (Rupees Twenty Eight Thousand only) and received Rs.7,000 (Rupees Seven Thousand only) as earnest money. This earnest money were paid by Mrs. Sultana Begum and the purchaser equally and were received by MA Quader and Monu Meah equally. Whereas MA Quader received Rs.10,500 (Rupees Ten Thousand Five Hundred only) and executed sale deed of his behalf share to Mrs. Sultana Begum and in the meantime Monu Meah died leaving his nine heirs — two wives — Noor Jahan Begum and Chemon Bahar, six sons —Mohd. maser, Mohd. Yousuf the vendors and both are major, Gulzar Hossain, Akter Hossain, Chand Meah, lshaque Meah, one dauthter - Anjuman Ara all are minor. Now whereas the vendors require money for their business and worldly expenses they, in pursuance of the sale agreement of their late father, decided to execute the sale deed of their portion of the land "
35. From the discussions made above, it is evident that the contract for sale executed between the defendant No.1 and Monu Meah has been proved by the admission of the heirs of said Monu Meah who deposed in this suit and also by the other documentary evidences which are annexed by firisti. Thus the observations of the trial court regarding the contract for sale as well as the Suit No.57 of 1967 which also affirmed by the appellate court below and by the High Court Division are not based upon the proper appreciation of the evidence on record.
36. This Division in the case of Sree Sree Modon Mohan Gouro Nitai Deva Bigraha vs Mozaharul Islam Chowahury, reported in 2008 (16) FELT (AD) 231, by referring the judgment and order dated 1-6-2005 passed by this Division in Civil Appeal No.283 of 2003, held that:
"The respondent already obtained a decree in his Title Suit No.404 of 1984 in which the present petitioner and pro-forma respondent No.2 were not parties. The Appellate Division under the facts and circumstances and in view of the materials on record held that the petitioner and pro-forma respondent No.2 have no locus-standi to file the suit alleging himself to be a shebait long after the delivery of possession of suit land to the respondent."
37. On perusal of evidence on record it appears that the defendant No.1 filed the original copy of registered Deed Nos.8567 and 5078 dated 28-6-1967 and 15-9-1966 which were marked as Exhibits A and A-1 respectively. Exhibits A and A-1 were executed by the heirs of Monu Meah and the deeds are thirty years old original documents submitted before the court from the proper custody and, as such, those deeds carries a presumption of correctness as per provision of section 90 of the Evidence Act. Moreover, the plaintiff of the instant suit as well as the executants of those deeds i.e. the heirs of the Monu Meah did not challenge the same as such the deeds which were marked as Exhibits A and A-1 stands as proper and genuine.
38. In this regard we need to refer section 90 of the Evidence Act, which is as under:
"90. Presumption as to documents thirty years old: Where any document, purporting or proved to be thirty years old, is produced from any custody which the court in the particular case considers proper, the Court may presume that the signature and every other part of such document, which purports to be in the handwriting of any particular person, is in that person's handwriting, and, in the case of a document executed or attested, that it was duly executed and attested by the person by whom it purports to be executed and attested."
39. The executants of said deed as well as the defendants of Suit No.57 of 1967 are still alive and they did not repudiate the same in any court after attaining majority.
40. Article 44 of the Limitation Act prescribes the period of limitation of suit by a ward that has attained majority to set-aside a transfer of property by his guardian.
41. Article 14 of the Limitation Act runs as under:
Description of suit	Period of limitation 	Time from which period begins to run
44. By a ward who has attained majority, to set-aside a transfer of property by his guardian. 	Part VI-Three Years (contd.)
Three years 	When the ward attains majority
42. The High Court of Calcutta in the case of Lalit Kumar Chaudhury and others vs Nogendra Lal Das and others, reported in AIR 1940 Cal 589, observed that:
"A suit by their vendor to set-aside the transfer was already barred before their purchase. In such circumstances the appellants' suit would fail not because their right was extinguished under section 28 but because their conveyance was defeated by an earlier conveyance which could no longer be impugned."
43. From the principle enunciated in the cited case, it appears that as the heirs of Monu Meah after attaining majority did not repudiate the Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 in any court of law as such the conveyance of the present plaintiff was defeated by an earlier conveyance i.e. the Deed No.8684 dated 12-104974 which could no longer be impugned by the present plaintiff and, as such, it appears that the genuineness of Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 is proved.
44. The trial court in his judgment and decree observed that:
“অতএব ১নং বিবাদীপক্ষকে প্রমাণ করিতে হইবে যে, আইনের বিধান মোতাবেক প্রদঃ এ, এ(১), এ(২) সম্পাদন করা হইয়াছে।”
45. But the trial court misconstrued the provisions of the Evidence Act inasmuch as the documents which were marked as Exhibits A, A-1 and A-2 carries a presumption of their correctness as per provision of section 90 of the Evidence Act which is discussed earlier. In this context the person who denied the correctness of those deeds, burden of disproving the same is lies upon him/her according to the provisions of the Evidence Act. Though the plaintiff denied the same but they did not take any step to disprove those deeds.
46. Plaintiff claimed that the heirs of Monu Meah sold the suit land of 10.50 Gondas in her favour by three registered deeds dated 14-5-1980 and 15-5-1980 respectively.
47. In this context it may be mentioned here that after transfer of suit land of 10.50 Gondas on or before 12-10-1974 by the heirs of Monu Meah infavour of defendant No.1, the title of the heirs of Monu Meah were extinguished and thus the heirs of Monu Meah have no saleable interest in the suit land on or after 12-10-1974. Thus, the heirs of Monu Meah after losing their title over the suit land sold the same by three deeds in 1980 infavour of the plaintiff and therefore, the plaintiff did not acquire any title in the suit land.
48. Moreover, the time from which a registered document operates is discussed in section 47 of the Registration Act which is as under:
"47. Time from which registered documents operates: A registered documents shall operate from the time which it would have commenced to operate if no registration thereof had been required or made, and not from the time of its registration."
49. This division in the case of Rafiqul Islam (Md) vs Mir Abdul Ali, reported in 44 DLR (AD) 176, observed:
"When the same vendor executes and registers two sale deeds in respect of the same suit land infavour of two different purchasers on two different dates, section 47 of the Registration Act settles which one will prevail over the other. The sale deed which was executed earlier but registered later in point of time will prevail over the sale deed executed later but registered earlier in point of time and the criterion in such cases for the purpose of determining when the sale takes effect is not the date of registration but the date of execution of the sale deed itself."
<u>50. Considering the above discussions and the principles enunciated in the referred cases, we are of the view that the plaintiff miserably failed to prove their title over the suit land, as such, they are not entitled to get a preliminary decree in the instant partition suit. Furthermore, the present suit is not maintainable in its present form without a prayer for recovery of khas possession as well as not impugning the Deed Nos.8567, 5078 dated 28-6-1967 and 15-9-1966 respectively. Beside this the plaintiff is also bound by the judgment and decree of Suit No.57 of 1967 passed by the learned Sub-Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong. As such the instant suit is liable to be dismissed.</u>
51. Both the trial Court and Appellate Court below after discussing the evidence on record arrived at a finding that the respondent No.5 is entitled to get saham of 9 (nine and one-fourth) Gondas of land in RS Plot No.127. The High Court Division concurred with the findings of the trial Court as well as the Appellate Court below. Since the plaintiff allegedly purchased the land from the heirs of Monu Meah and claiming partition of the said land, as such, there is no dispute regarding the portion of the land belonged to MA Quader which was after transfer possessed by the respondent No.5.
52. But the trial court without considering this legal and factual aspect and without appreciating the evidence on record erroneously decreed the Other Class Suit No.179 of 1980 renumbered as Suit No.225 of 1990 which was affirmed by the appellate court below in Appeal Case No.365 of 2002 as well as by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4785 of 2003 and thus calls for interference by this Division.
53. We have perused the cases cited by the learned advocate for respondent Nos. 1-3 but we do not find applicability of the same in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
54. Thus, the appeal is allowed.
55. Accordingly, preliminary decree passed allocating saham of 9¼ (nine and one-fourth) Gondas land to the heirs of defendant No.1- appellant in RS Plot No.127 and respondent No.5 (defendant No.3 in the suit) is allocated rest 9¼ (nine and one-fourth) Gondas in RS Plot No.127 of the suit schedule land which will take effect within 30(thirty) days from date amicably, otherwise the parties are entitled to get saham through court.
56. The judgment and decree dated 24-7-2002 and 14-8-2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong, in Other Class Suit No.179 of 1980 renumbered as 225 of 1990 and also affirmed by the learned Additional District Judge (In-charge), 6th Court, Chittagong, in Other Class Appeal No.365 of 2002 and by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4785 of 2003 vide judgment and order dated 18-1-2010 are hereby set-aside.
However, no order as to costs.
End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 13th of February 2014 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 1606-1612).
full_judgment:
M. Enayetur Rahim, J: These civil appeals, by leave, are directed against the judgment and order dated 13-2-2014 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos.1606-1612 of 2010 making the Rules absolute. All the appeals have been heard together and they are being disposed of by this common judgment.
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of these appeals, in short, are that the petitioner in writ petition No. 1606 of 2010, presently respondent was appointed as "Receptionist" and petitioners in writ Petition Nos. 1607-1611 of 2010, presently respondents were appointed as "NESS" and the petitioner in Writ petition No. 1612 of 2010, presently respondent was appointed as "Proof Reader" of Bangladesh Parliament Secretariat following the Recruitment Rules of Bangladesh Sangshad Sachibaloy, 1994.
3. In the writ petitions, it was contended that in response to the advertisement published in the Daily Newspapers inviting application for several posts for the office of Bangladesh Parliament Secretariat, the writ petitioners applied for their respective vacant posts. Written examination and viva-voce was held and upon duly concluding all the appointment procedure, the writ petitioners received their respective appointment letters as probationary employee for a period of 2 (two) years. After successful completion of two years probationary period they were confirmed effective from the date of their joining in the said service considering their satisfactory performance under Rule 6(3)(Ka) of the Sangshad Sachibaloya, Employees and Officers Appointment Rules, 1994.
4. All of a sudden the writ respondent No. 2 issued a letter dated 18-2-2010 relieving all the writ petitioners from their respective services.
5. Being aggrieved by the said order dated 18-2-2010 all the writ petitioners moved before the High Court Division by filing different writ petitions.
6. A Division Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing all the Rules together by a common judgment and order dated 13-2-2014 made all the Rules absolute.
7. Feeling aggrieved by the said judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the writ-respondents as petitioners filed Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal Nos. 1519, 1522- 1526 and 1530 of 2014 before this Division and leave was granted on 7-2-2016. Hence, these appeals.
8. Mr AM Amin Uddin, learned Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division erred in law in failing to appreciate that the impugned order was issued pursuant to a decision adopted in a proceeding of the Parliament on the basis of recommendations made by a Parliamentary Committee formed by the Speaker under Article 76(2)(C)(d) of the Constitution as well as under Rules laid down in the chapter XXVI of the Rules of Procedure of Parliament to enquire into the allegations relating to corruption, misuse of power, wastage of public fund by the then Speaker, Barrister Mohammad Jamiruddin Sirker, and the Proceedings of the Parliament is immured from challenge under Article 78 of the Constitution and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside.
9. Learned Attorney-General further submits that as per section 14 of the Sangsad Sachibaloy Act, 1994, the Speaker is answerable to the National Parliament for all functions and actions relating to National Parliament Secretariat and any decision of the National parliament taken in its proceedings having been immuned from challenge and in such view of the matter, the impugned order issued pursuant to the said proceedings cannot be called in question in any court of law. He also submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the recruitment process was void ab initio since Parliamentary Committee upon its enquiry found that the recruitment process of the respondents-writ petitioners was tainted with serious irregularities, corruption, misuse of power and violation of the injunction imposed by the then Ministry of Establishment committed by the then Speaker of 8th Parliament upon which the Parliament in its proceeding adopted a decision to cancel the said appointments and in such view of the matter, the writ petitioners accrued no vested right and they do not come under the ambit of the Service Rules of Sangsad Sachibalay, Namely, Sangsad Schibalay Karmokarta-o-Karmochary Neog Bidhimala, 1994 and Jatio sangsad Sachibalay Kormokarta-o-Karmochary (Sringkhola-o-Appeal) Bidhimala, 2005 and hence, no show cause notice or departmental proceedings is required to relieve the writ-petitioners from their service.
10. Learned Attorney-General also submits that the High Court Division erred in law in failing to appreciate that it is a settled principle of law that if the appointment is made without following the rules and procedure, no vested right is accrued and since the respondents-writ-petitioners got their respective appointment as a result of irregularities and corrupt practice, they have not therefore acquired any vested right in their service on such illegal appointments. Learned Attorney-General having referred to the case of Nuruzzaman (Arid) and others vs Bangladesh and others 64 DLR 406, Rina Rani Sutradhar and others vs Bangladesh 20 BLC (ADS 246 (para H), Pankaj Gupta vs The State of Jammu and Kahsmir reported in 8 SCC (2004) 353 and the Secretanj, State of Karnataka vs Umadevi (2006) 4 SCC 1) submits that the illegality and irregularity are so intermixed with the whole process of selection that it becomes impossible to sort-out right from wrong and vice versa, the rules of natural justice cannot be put in a Straight jacket [Md Fazle Rabbi Mia vs Professor Aftab Uddin Ahmed and others, 2 LNJJ (2013) 46] and, as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set-aside.
11. Per contra, Mr Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate and Mr Zulhas Uddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents made submissions in support of the impugned judgement and order of the High Court Division. In addition, it has been submitted that Article 78 of the Constitution only protects "proceedings of the parliament" from judicial review. The impugned orders do not come within the purview of parliamentary proceedings. It has been further submitted that the High Court Division categorically found the writ petitioners had "no hand" in the recruitment process. The Parliament Secretariat being independent and not being under any Ministry or Department of any Ministry, the appointments could not be held to be violative of any prohibitive order of the Ministry of Establishment and the appointments having been made in accordance with the provisions of the Bangladesh Parliament Secretariat Recruitment Rules 1994, the contention as to the petitioners' appointments being void ab-initio as propagated by the appellants does not have a sound leg to stand upon. For the same reason, the decision reported in 2 LNJ (2013) 46 as relied upon by the appellant in reason No. 4 are not at all attracted to the present case and, as such, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division does not call for any interference by this Division.
12. We have considered the rival submissions of the learned Advocates for the respective parties, perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and the materials as placed before us.
13. In the instant cases it is undeniable fact that the 9th Parliament in its 1st session on 19th March, 2009 adopted a resolution to make inquiry with regard to the illegalities and irregularities of the appointments, misuse of power, corruption, wastage of public fund by the then Speaker Barrister Mohammad Jamiruddin Sirker and the Speaker on that day on the basis of the decision adopted in the House, formed a 12 members inquiry committee amongst the Members of Parliament headed by Mr Md Fazle Rabbi Mia, MP (Gaibandha-5). The said parliamentary inquiry committee after holding inquiry placed its report before the Parliament making some recommendations. The relevant portion of the recommendations are as follows:
৩.৬ “কমিটির সিদ্ধান্ত/সুপারিশঃ
(ক) বাংলাদেশ জাতীয় সংসদ সচিবালয়ের জনবল নিয়োগের সাবেক স্পীকার ব্যারিস্টার মুহম্মদ জমির উদ্দিন সরকার কোটা না মেনে, বেআইনীভাবে বয়স প্রমার্জন করে, পুলিশী প্রতিবেদনে বিরূপ মন্তব্য থাকা সত্ত্বেও সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্মচারীদের চাকুরীতে বহাল রেখে, সংসদ চালু না থাকা সত্ত্বেও স্থায়ী পদে এম.এল.এস.এস নিয়োগ, সংসদীয় স্থায়ী কমিটি না থাকা সর্তেও তাদের ব্যক্তিগত সহকারীগণের চাকুরী ৩০-৬-২০০৭ পর্যস্ত বর্ধিত করে গুরুতর আর্থিক অনিয়ম করেছেন। এছাড়া তিনি দেশে বিদ্যমান আইন কানুন এবং সংবিধানের অপব্যাখ্যা দিয়ে স্বেচ্ছাচারিতার আশ্রয় গ্রহণ করেছেন এবং ক্ষমতার চরম অপব্যবহার করেছেন। যার ফলে পবিত্র জাতীয় সংসদের মর্যাদা জনমানসে ভূলুষ্ঠিত হয়েছে। তিনি তার শপথের মর্যাদা ক্ষুণ্ন করেছেন। সাবেক স্পীকারের এ জাতীয় স্বেচ্ছাচারি ক্ষমতার অপব্যবহার দুনীতি, গুরুতর আর্থিক অনিয়ম এবং সরকারী অর্থ অপচয়ের বিষয়ে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণের জন্য এ কমিটি সুপারিশ করছে।
(খ) কোটা না মানা, বেআইনীভাবে বয়স প্রমার্জন করে নিয়োগের ক্ষেত্রে সহায়তা দানকারী সংসদ সচিবালয়ের সংশ্লিষ্ট বাছাই কমিটি ও জড়িত অন্যান্য কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারীগণের বিষয়ে আইনগত সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণের জন্য কমিটি সুপারিশ করছে।
(গ) কোটা না মেনে যাদেরকে নিয়োগ দেয়া হয়েছে তাদের ব্যাপারে আইনানুগ সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণের জন্য কমিটি সুপারিশ করছে।
(ঘ) বিরূপ পুলিশি প্রতিবেদন থাকা সত্তেও সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্মচারীদের চাকুরী বহাল রাখার সাথে যে সকল কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারী জড়িত তাদের বিষয়ে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণের জন্য কমিটি সুপারিশ করছে।
(ঙ) সংসদ না থাকা সত্তেও কমিটির সভাপতিগণের জন্য স্থায়ী পদে ৪২ জন এম.এল,.এস.এস নিয়োগ এবং সংসদীয় কমিটি না থাকা সত্তেও সভাপতিগণের জন্য নিয়োজিত ব্যক্তিগত সরকারীদের চাকুরী ৩০-৬-২০০৭ পর্যন্ত বর্ধিত করে এবং তাদের বেতন ভাতা প্রদান করে সর্বমোট ৬২,৯৯,১৭৯/২৭ (বাষ্টি লক্ষ নিরানব্বই হাজার একশত উনাশি টাকা সাতাশ পয়সা সরকারী অর্থের যে অপচয় করা হয়েছে সে সম্পর্কে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণের জন্য কমিটি সুপারিশ করছে।
৩.৭ সার্বিক মন্তব্যঃ
২নং সংসদীয় সাব কমিটির সদস্যবৃন্দ কমিটি বৈঠকে উপস্থিত থেকে তাদের সক্রিয় অংশগ্রহণ এবং গুরুতত্পূর্ণ মতামত প্রদান করে রিপোর্ট প্রণয়নে অনন্য অবদান রেখেছেন । দুীতিমুক্ত একটি গণমুখী রাষ্ট্র ব্যবস্থা কায়েমে প্রশাসনে স্বচ্ছতা, জবাবদিহিতা এবং সুশাসন প্রতিষ্ঠার কোন বিকল্প নেই। উন্নয়নমুখী প্রশাসন এবং শক্তিশালী গণতান্ত্রিক মূল্যবোধ প্রতিষ্ঠার মূল চাবিকাঠি হলো সুশাসন। ২নং সংসদীয় সাব কমিটির মাননীয় সদস্যবৃন্দ মনে করেন এ কমিটির গৃহীত সিদ্ধান্ত ও সুপারিশসমূহ বাস্তবায়িত হলে প্রশাসনে স্বচ্ছতা, জবাবদিহিতা ও সুশাসন প্রতিষ্ঠার ক্ষেত্রে উল্লেখযোগ্য অগ্রগতি সাধিত হবে ।”
14. On 13-10-2009 a good number of Members of Parliament including both ruling party and the oppositions discussed on the said report. At the time of discussion on the report, various suggestions and recommendations were given by the Members of Parliament and ultimately, the report was accepted by the House.
15. The relevant proceedings of the Parliament is as follows:
“সংসদী���় তদন্ত কমিটির রিপোর্ট সম্পর্কে সংসদ কর্তৃক সর্বসম্মতিক্রমে গৃহীত সিদ্ধান্ত ।
মাননীয় সদস্যবৃন্দ, সংসদীয় তদন্ত কমিটির রিপোর্ট সম্পর্কে এতক্ষণ মাননীয় সংসদ-সদস্যগণ যে সকল বক্তব্য এবং প্রস্তাব পেশ করেছেন তৎসম্পর্কে –আমার বক্তব্য হল-সংসদে আপনাকে দাবীর প্রেক্ষিতে আপনাকে Sentiment এর প্রতি শ্রদ্ধা জানিয়ে জাতীয় সংসদ সচিবালয়ে সংঘটিত অনিয়ম, দুননীতি, সরকারি অর্থ আত্মসাৎ ইত্যাদি বিষয়ে তদন্তের জন্য বিগত ১৯শে মার্চ ২০০৯ তারিখে এই সংসদীয় তদন্ত কমিটি গঠন করা হয়েছিল। এই কমিটির রিপোর্টের উপর আপনারা যে আলোচনা করেছেন তা আমি মনোযোগ দিয়ে শুনেছি। আশা করি আপনারাও শুনেছেন।
এখানে আমি বলতে চাই, আমাদের দেশে সংসদীয় গণতন্ত্রের চর্চা দীর্ঘ সময়ের নয় গণতান্ত্রিক ব্যবস্থা সফলভাবে কার্যকর করার জন্য আমাদের দেশে যে সকল গনতান্ত্রিক প্রতিষ্ঠান রয়েছে, সেগুলোকে দুর্নীতি, অনিয়ম ইত্যাদি থেকে যুক্ত রাখতে হবে। জাতীয় সংসদ এ দেশের সর্ববৃহৎ গণতান্ত্রিক প্রতিষ্ঠান। জনগণ এ প্রতিষ্ঠানের মাধ্যমে সরকারকে তাদের নিকট জবাবদিহি করতে বাধ্য করে। জাতীয় সংসদ-কে দায়িত্ব পালনে সহায়তা করার জন্য প্রতিষ্ঠিত হয়েছে জাতীয় সংসদ সচিবালয়। এ সচিবালয়কে সকল দুর্নীতির উর্ধ্বে রেখে নজির প্রতিষ্ঠার জন্য আমাদের সকলকে সর্বদা সচেষ্ট থাকতে হবে।
তদন্ত রিপোর্টের বিষয়ে আপনারা যে আলোচনা করেছেন সে বিষয়ে কি করণীয় তা সংসদে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণের মাধ্যমে আপনারাই ঠিক করবেন । একটি বিষয়ে আমি আপনাদের দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ করতে চাই। কমিটির তদন্ত রিপোর্টের সমন্বিত সুপারিশসমূহের মধ্যে সাবেক মাননীয় স্পীকার ব্যারিস্টার মুহম্মদ জমির উদ্দিন সরকারের ৯ম জাতীয় সংসদের সদস্য পদ খারিজ করার সুপারিশ করা হয়েছে। এই সুপারিশটি আমাদের দেশের প্রেক্ষাপটে আমার কাছে অতি কঠোর বলে মনে হচ্ছে। কমিটি এরূপ সুপারিশের সমর্থনে ভারত, কানাডা ও যুক্তরাজ্যের সংসদীয় রীতি-নীতির উল্লেখ করেছে। আমাদের সংবিধানে বা জাতীয় সংসদের কার্যপ্রণালী-বিধি অথবা বিদ্যমান বিধি-বিধানে একজন মাননীয় স্পীকারের তদন্ত রিপোর্টে উল্লিখিত দুর্নীতি, অনিয়মের জন্য সংসদ-সদস্য পদ খারিজ করার সুস্পষ্ট কোনো বিধান নেই। আমাদের দেশের সংসদীয় গনতন্ত্রের ইতিহাসে ঐ সব ফারণে সংসদ-সদস্য পদ বাতিলের কোনো নজিরও নেই। এ দেশের উন্নত গণতান্ত্রিক ব্যবস্থা চূড়ান্ত উৎকর্ষ সাধন হলে সে সময় অন্যান্য দেশের ন্যায় এরূপ বিষয়ে বিবেচনা করে দেখা যেতে পারে । এ পর্যায়ে সংসদ সদস্য পদ বাতিলের সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করা যথাযথ হবে না বলে আমি মনে করি ।
মাননীয় সদস্যবৃন্দ, আশা করি আপনারাও আমার সাথে একমত পোষণ করবেন। কাজেই মাননীয় সংসদ-সদস্য জনাব রাশেদ খান মেনন কার্যপ্রণালী বিধির ২৯২ বিধি অনুযায়ী যে প্রস্তাব এনেছেন তন্মধ্যে সাবেক মাননীয় স্পীকার, ব্যারিস্টার মুহম্মদ জমির উদ্দিন সরকারের ৯ম জাতীয় সংসদের সদস্য পদ খারিজ করা সংক্রান্ত প্রস্তাব ব্যতীত অন্যান্য প্রস্তাবগুলো আমি এখন ভোটে দিচ্ছি।
সংসদের সামনে প্রশ্ন হচ্ছে,
মাননীয় সংসদ-সদস্য জনাব রাশেদ মেনন কার্যপ্রণালী বিধির ২৯২ বিধি অনুযাধী যে প্রস্তাব এনেছেন তন্মধ্যে সাবেক মাননীয় ' স্পীকার ব্যারিস্টার মুহম্মদ জমিরউদ্দিন সরকারের ৯ম জাতীয় সংসদের সদস্য পদ খারিজ করা সংক্রান্ত প্রস্তাব ব্যতীত অন্যান্য প্রস্তাবগুলো গ্রহণ করা হউক ।
যাঁরা এ প্রস্তাবের পক্ষে আছেন, তারা “হ্যা” বলুন ।
[ধ্বনিভোট গ্রহণের পর-]
যাঁরা এ প্রস্তাবের বিপক্ষে আছেন, তারা “না”বলুন ।
[ধ্বনিভোট গ্রহণের পর-]
আমার মনে হয়, “হ্যা” জয়যুক্ত হয়েছে “হ্যা” জয়যুক্ত হয়েছে, “হ্যা” জয়যুক্ত হয়েছে।
অতএব, সাবেক মাননীয় স্পীকার ব্যারিস্টার মুহম্মদ জমিরউদ্দিন সরকারের ৯ম জাতীয় সংসদের সংসদ সদস্য পদ খারিজ করা সংক্রান্ত প্রস্তাব ব্যতীত অন্যান্য প্রস্তাবগুলো সংসদে সর্বসম্মতিক্রমে গৃহীত হলো ।”
16. It is pertinent to mention here that Mr Rashed Khan Manon, MP proposed to adopt the following proposal under rule 292 of the ‘বাংলাদেশ জাতীয় সংসদ কার্যপ্রণালী-বিধি’:
“(ক) সাবেক মাননীয় স্পীকার ব্যারিস্টার মুহম্মদ জমির উদ্দিন সরকার, সাবেক ডেপুটি স্বীকার জনাব আখতার হামিদ সিদ্দিকী এবং সাবেক চীফ হুইপ খোন্দকার দেলোয়ার হোসেন অনিয়ম ও দুর্নীতি করে অর্থ আত্মসাৎ এবং অপচয় করে সরকারের যে আর্থিক ক্ষতি করেছেন তা আইনী ব্যবস্থা হণের মাধ্যমে তাদের নিকট থেকে আদায় করা হউক:
খে) সাবেক মাননীয় স্পীকার ব্যারিস্টার মুহম্মদ জমির উদ্দিন সরকার সরকারি বিধি বিধান অমান্য করে নিয়ম বহির্ভূত পন্থায় যে সকল কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারী নিয়োগ দিয়েছেন সে সকল নিয়োগ বাতিল করা হউক:”
17. Pursuant to the said resolution of the parliament, the Secretariat of Bangladesh Jatio Sangshad cancelled the appointment of the respective writ petitioners vide its official letter on 18-2-2010.
18. Learned Attorney-General candidly submits that since the impugned order was issued pursuant to a decision adopted in a proceeding of the Parliament on the basis of the recommendation made by the Parliamentary Committee, formed by the Speaker under Article 76 (2)(c)(d) of the Constitution as well as under the Rules laid down in Chapter XXIV of the Rules of Parliament as such the proceedings as well as the decision taken on the basis of such proceedings is immuned from judicial review as per provision of Article 78 of the Constitution.
19. The Article 78(1) of the Constitution speaks as follows:
“সংসদের কার্যধারার বৈধতা সম্পর্কে কোন আদালতে প্রশ্ন উত্থাপন করা যাইবে না।”
[The validity of the proceedings in parliament shall not be questioned in any Court].
20. Mr Probir Neogi, Learned Senior Advocate, appearing for the writ petitioners-respondents submits that in the instant cases since the service of the writ petitioners-respondents have been made permanent following the relevant Service Rules, and since they have been serving for a quite long period, they cannot be dismissed from the service without following the relevant Service Rule, i.e. সংসদ সচিবালয় কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারী নিয়োগ বিধিমালা, ১৯৯৪ and the doctrine of parliamentary privilege will not be applicable in these particular cases.
21. In view of Article 78(1) of our Constitution the proceedings in Parliament shall not be questioned in any Court.
22. However, a pertinent question is required to be addressed that in what circumstances and situations Court can exercise its power under judicial review on a Parliamentary proceeding, and how far its proceeding is immuned from judicial review.
23. In the case of Raza Ram Paul vs Honb'le Speaker, Loksobha IMANLI/SC/0241/2007 = Supreme Court Cases, 2007, Vol. III (2007) 3 SCC page-184J, the Supreme Court of India has dealt with the issue of parliamentary privilege and having considered of its earlier various judgments/decisions held that no power is absolute but subject to checks and balances and judicial review. In the said case, the Supreme Court of India has formulated the principles relating to the parameters of judicial review in relation to the exercise of parliamentary provisions:
"Summary of the principles relating to parameters of judicial review in relation to exercise of parliamentary provisions:
431. We may summarise the principles that can be culled out from the above discussion. They are:
(a) Parliament is a coordinate organ and its views do deserve deference even while its acts are amenable to judicial scrutiny;
(b) The constitutional system of government abhors absolutism and it being the cardinal principle of our Constitution that no one, howsoever lofty, can claim to be the sole judge of the power given under the Constitution mere coordinate constitutional status or even the  status of an exalted constitutional  functionaries, does not disentitle  this Court from exercising its  jurisdiction of judicial review of actions which partake the character of judicial or quasi-judicial decision;
(c) The expediency and necessity of exercise of power or privilege by the legislature are for the determination of the legislative authority and not for determination by the courts;
(d) The judicial review of the manner of exercise of power of contempt or privilege does not mean the said jurisdiction is being usurped by the judicature;
(e) Having regard to the importance of the functions discharged by the legislature under the Constitution and the majesty and grandeur of its task, there would always be an initial presumption that the powers, privileges, etc. have been regularly and reason-ably exercised, not violating the law or the constitutional provisions, this presumption being a rebuttable one;
(f) The fact that Parliament is an august body of co-ordinate constitutional position does not mean that there can be no judicially manageable standards to review exercise of its power;
(g) While the area of powers, privileges and immunities of the legislature being exceptional and extraordinary its acts, particularly relating to exercise thereof, ought not to be tested on the traditional parameters of judicial review in the same manner as an ordinary administrative action would be tested, and the Court would confine itself to the acknowledged parameters of judicial review and within the judicially discoverable and manageable standards, there is no foundation to the plea that a legislative body cannot be attributed jurisdictional error;
(h) The judicature is not prevented from scrutinising the validity of the action of the legislature trespassing on the fundamental rights conferred on the citizens.
(i) The broad contention that the exercise of privileges by legislatures cannot be decided against the touchstone of fundamental rights or the constitutional provisions is not correct;
(j) If a citizen, whether a non-Member or a Member of the legislature, complains that his fundamental rights under Article 20 or 21 had been contravened, it is the duty of this Court to examine the merits of the said  contention, especially when the impugned action entails civil consequences;
(k) There is no basis to the claim of bar of exclusive cognizance or absolute immunity to the parliamentary proceedings in Article 105(3) of the Constitution; (l) The manner of enforcement of privilege by the legislature can result in judicial scrutiny, though subject to the restrictions contained in the other constitutional provisions, for example Article 122 or 212;
(m) Article 122(1) and Article 212(1) displace the broad doctrine of exclusive cognizance of the legislature in England of exclusive cognizance of internal proceedings of the House rendering irrelevant the case-law that emanated from courts in that jurisdiction; inasmuch as the same has no application to the system of governance provided by the Constitution of India;
(n) Article 122(1) and Article 212(1) prohibit the validity of any proceedings in legislature from being called in question in a court merely on the ground of irregularity of procedure;
(o) The truth or correctness of the material will not be questioned by the court nor will it go into the adequacy of the material or substitute its opinion for that of the legislature;
(p) Ordinarily, the legislature, as a body, cannot be accused of having acted for an extraneous purpose or being actuated by caprice or mala fide intention, and the court will not lightly presume abuse or misuse, giving allowance for the fact that the legislature is the best judge of such matters, but if in a given case the allegations to such effect are made, the court may examine the validity of the said contention the onus on the person alleging being extremely heavy;
(q) The rules which the legislature has to make for regulating its procedure and the conduct of its business have to be subject to the provisions of the Constitution;
(r) Mere availability of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business, as made by the legislature in exercise of enabling powers under the Constitution, is never a guarantee that they have been duly followed;
(s) The proceedings which may be tainted on account of substantive or gross illegality or unconstitutionality are not protected from judicial scrutiny;
(t) Even if some of the material on which the action is taken is found to be irrelevant, the court would still not interfere so long as there is some relevant material sustaining the action;
(u) An ouster clause attaching finality to a determination does ordinarily oust the power of the court to review the decision but not on grounds of lack of jurisdiction or it being a nullity for some reason such as gross illegality, irrationality, violation of constitutional mandate, mala fides, non-compliance with rules of natural justice and perversity.
432. It can now be examined if the manner of exercise of the power of expulsion hi the cases at hand suffers from any such illegality or unconstitutionality as to call for interference by this Court."
24. In view of the above propositions, Courts power of judicial review on the proceedings of Parliament is not absolutely ousted. In certain facts and circumstance, in particular on the grounds of lack of jurisdiction or it being a nullity for some reasons, such as, gross illegality, irrationality, violation of constitutional mandate, malafides, non-compliance with rules of natural justice and perversity, Court has the jurisdiction to exercise its power under judicial review.
25. Let us now consider the submissions of learned Attorney-General in the light of the above principles coupled with the facts and circumstances of the present case.
26. From the facts as it reveals in the instant cases that the Parliament in its sessions adopted a resolution to make inquiry with regard to the alleged illegal and irregular appointments made by the then Speaker Mohammad Jamiruddin Sirker and accordingly, an inquiry committee was formed. Thereafter, the said inquiry committee after holding an inquiry placed its report before the Parliament and an open discussion was held on the said inquiry report by the members of Parliament and, thereafter, the Speaker put the resolution proposed by Mr Rashed Khan Manon, MP before the House for adoption and the House had adopted the said resolution cancelling all the illegal appointments, and pursuant to the said resolution, the impugned order has been issued and communicated by the Parliament Secretariat to the respective writ petitioners. The learned Advocates for the writ petitioners-respondents have failed to show us that in taking such recourse by the Parliament, the Parliament or the Speaker has violated any rule of Rules of Procedure of Parliament as well as the Constitution. The House and the inquiry committee discussed various aspects on the issue in question. Since the Constitution and Rules of Procedure have not been violated in the proceeding of Parliament, it is our considered view that there is no scope of judicial review to adjudicate the propriety of the said proceedings and resolution adopted by the Parliament and, as such, we have no hesitation to accept the submission of the learned Attorney-General that in these particular cases the impugned decision and the above proceedings of the Parliament is immuned to be questioned before any Court.
27. The learned Advocates for the writ petitioners-respondents have tried to convince us that before taking the impugned action cancelling the appointments of the respective respondents, they were not given any opportunity of being heard and thereby principle of natural justice has been violated, since their service has been confirmed by the authority as per relevant Service Rules.
28. It is now well settled that if the appointments have been made without following the Rules of Procedure, the concerned employees have not acquired any vested right in the office on the basis of such irregular and illegal appointment. In the case of Nuruzzaman Md and others vs Bangladesh and others, reported in 64 DLR 406 it has been held that:
"Since the appointments have been made without following the rules and procedures, and in the inquiry report it has been opined that the petitioners managed to get their appointments by way of irregularities and corrupt practice, we are of the view that the petitioners have not acquired any vested right in the office on the basis of their appointments. There is no illegality and irregularity in the order of cancellation as made by the respondents".
29. The High Court Division in making the above observations relied on the case of Pankaj Gupta vs the State of Jammu and Kashmir, reported in 8 SCC (2004) 353, wherein it has been held that: "No person illegally appointed or appointed without following the procedure prescribed under the law is entitled to claim that he should be continue in the service."
30. The above judgment of the High Court Division has been affirmed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to appeal No. 245-152 of 2003, reported in 20 BLC (AD) 246 wherein this Division has held that:
"Considering the report of the inquiry committee, the Government cancelled the order of appointments and that it could not be said that letter impugned before the High Court Division was arbitrary. The High Court Division further found that the appointments had been made without following the rules and procedures and that in the inquiry report it had been opined that the petitioners managed to get their appointments by way of irregularities and corrupt practice. The High Court Division also found that the petitioners had not acquired any vested right in the office on the basis of their appointments. Therefore, the High Court Division concluded that there was no illegality or irregularity in the order of cancellation made by the respondents.
The finding of the High Court Division having been based on proper appreciation of law and fact do not call for interference."
31. In the case of Md Fazle Rabbi Mia vs Aftab Uddin Ahmed and others, reported in 2 LNJ (2013) 46, a Division Bench of the High Court Division has held that-there is no violation of the rules of natural justice wherein illegalities, irregularities, arbitrariness and abuse of power in the process of creating of posts, selection and appointments are so intermixed that it becomes impossible to sort out the right from wrong and vice versa.
32. In the case of Krishan Yadav and others vs State of Haryana and others [Manu/SC/0456/1994J the Supreme Court of India having found that the selection was done without interview, fake and ghost interviews, tempering with the final records, fabricating documents and forgery has observed as under:
"It is highly regrettable that the holders of public offices both big and small have forgotten that the offices entrusted to them are sacred trusts. Such offices are meant for use and not abuse. From a Minister to a menial everyone has been dishonest to gain undue advantages. The whole examination and the interview have turned out to be farcical exhibiting base character of those who have been responsible for this sordid episode. It shocks our conscience to come across such a systematic fraud. It is somewhat surprising the High Court should have taken the path of least resistance stating in view of the destruction of records it was helpless: It should have helped itself. Law is not that powerless.
In the above circumstances, what are we to do? The only proper courses open to us is to set-aside the entire selection. The plea was made that innocent candidates should not be penalised for the misdeeds of others. We are unable to accept this argument. When the entire selection is stinking, conceived in fraud and delivered in deceit, individual innocence has no place as "Fraud unravels everything". To put it in other words, the entire selection is arbitrary. It is that which is faulted and not the individual candidates. Accordingly we hereby set-aside the selection of Taxation Inspectors.
The effect of setting aside the selection would mean the appointments held by these 96 candidates (including the respondents) will have no right to go to the office. Normally speaking, we should require them to disgorge the benefit of these ill-gotten gains. That means they will have to repay the entire salary and perks which they have received from the said office. But, here we show a streak of sympathy. For more than 4 years they were enjoying the benefit of "office". The proper lesson would be learnt by them if their appointments are set-aside teaching them that dishonesty could never pay.
All these efforts by us are aimed at cleansing the public administration. No doubt, it may be stupendous task but we do hope this small step will make great strides in the days to come. Accordingly, the appeals stand allowed." (Underlines supplied).
33. In the case of Union of India vs JN Sinha (MANU/SC/0500/1970) the Supreme Court of India held that rules of natural justice are not attracted in such a case where the appropriate authority forms the requisite opinion bona fide and its opinion cannot be challenged before the Cowls. In the case of Baikantha Nath Das and others vs Chief District Medical Officer, Baripada and others [MANU/SC/0193/1992] it has been held that as action had been taken on subjective satisfaction of Government, there is no room for importing facet of natural justice in such a case.
34. In view of the above propositions, we are unable to accept the submission of Mr Neogi that in cancelling the order of appointments of the writ petitioners, which were the result of corrupt, illegal and male practice, the principle of natural justice has been violated.
35. In the case of Jagit Singh vs State of Hariyana, reported in (2006) 11 SCC 1, the Supreme Court of India has held that the principles of natural justice are not immutable but are flexible: they cannot be cast in a rigid module and put in a strait-jacket and the compliance therewith has to be considered in the facts and circumstances of each case.
36. Section 5(1) and section 14 of the জাতীয় সংসদ সচিবালয় আইন, ১৯৯৪ are as follows:
“সংসদ সচিবালয়ের কর্তৃত্ব-৫(১) সংসদ সচিবালয়ের প্রশাসনিক দায়িত্ব স্পীকারের উপর ন্যস্ত থাকিবে।
and
সংসদের নিকট স্পীকারের দায়িত্ব-১৪। সংসদ সচিবালয়ের যাবতীয় কর্মকান্ডের জন্য স্পীকার সংসদের নিকট দায়ী থাকিবেন।”
37. This Division in the case of Mayes jasmin and others vs Ruhul Amin, reported in 26 BLC (AD) 239 has observed that:
"The ordinary rule of construction of a statute must be construed in accordance with the language used depending upon the context. The Court should adopt purposive interpretation of the statute to articulate the felt necessities of the time. Article 79 of the constitution has been provided with the object that the Secretariat attached to the parliament should have staff, which should be under the effective control with the head of the parliament. The idea is to crystallise the position regarding supremacy of the Speaker and to give constitutional authority. The Speaker is the framer, operator and interpreter of the Rules and consequently he can amend the Rules from time to time following the related laws."
<u>38. If we consider the provisions of sections 5(1) and 14 of the জাতীয় সংসদ সচিবালয় আইন, ১৯৯৪ coupled with above proposition of law, then it would be abundantly clear that the Speaker of the Parliament has been entrusted with all the administrative power of the Parliament Secretariat but at the same time he</u>
<u>or she is answerable to the House for his or her conduct and activities relating to ‘সংসদ সচিবালয়ের যাবতীয় কর্মকান্ড’ and, as such, the House in taking the action on the illegal conduct/ activities of the Ex-Speaker did not violate any Rules of Procedure of the Parliament or any provision of the Constitution.</u>
39. Having considered and discussed above, we find merit in all the appeals. Accordingly, all the appeals are allowed. The impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is set-aside.
However, there is no order as to costs.
End.
